title: Storytelling

script.script:
My husband cheated on me with a model, so I became one at his agency at 51.

It started with what I saw backstage in Milan.

My husband is a photographer.

He shoots for a modeling agency, Runway Girls.

The billboard's on Sunset and he's beautiful.

He's the beautiful one, I'm the wife.

He doesn't wonder how I am anymore.

There was a video from vacation.

I watched it for minutes.

He was laughing.

He hadn't laughed with me in years.

And he touched her the way he hasn't touched me since 29.

Twenty two years.

He never once filmed me.

I didn't cry.

I didn't throw the camera.

I just drove to the grocery store because we needed milk.

That night I did what I hadn't done in years.

I really looked at myself in the mirror and I thought if I were him, I'd have picked her too.

Backstage in Milan.

Champagne, chaos, three hours of sleep.

Every single one of them, before hair, before makeup, they did the same thing.

Gina said, you think they wake up like that?

This is the first thing they do.

The part nobody shows.

She put a small box in my hand.

What is it?

What they use between shows.

What keeps them draining when nobody's watching.

I said, Gina, I'm 30 pounds too heavy for this.

I'm bloated all the time.

I need to lose weight.

She looked at me.

You're not heavy.

At 51, your estrogen drops.

Your lymphatic system slows down.

Your body stops draining naturally.

No more pushing the waste out.

So every glass of wine, every old hormone, every bit of inflammation.

It just sits there.

Pools in your belly.

Thickens.

Hardens.

That's the bloat.

That's the puffy face.

It's not fat.

It's waste that never left your body.

So what do I do?

You can't burn bloat.

You have to drain it.

Haven & Spool castor oil pack.

You wrap it around your belly every night.

The ricinoleic acid soaks through your skin while you sleep.

Opens the drainage channels.

And your body starts letting go.

Gina, I'm 51, I don't think—

Six weeks.

By week two, you'll feel different.

By week three, your face comes back.

By week six, you won't recognize yourself.

Trust it.

That first night, I wrapped the pack around my belly.

Felt like a warm hug.

I slept nine hours straight.

Week one, my body started moving.

Years of constipation, gone.

My cheeks came down first.

The puffiness just dissolved.

My ring slid off in the shower.

Week two, belt one notch tighter.

The belly that showed up at 48.

The one I carried for three years.

It started releasing.

I stopped hiding from photos.

Week three, jawline back.

Cheekbones sharp. 

Skin glowing like I remember.

Sleeping through the night.

Energy I hadn't felt since my 40s.

Week four, the fog lifted.

Names came back.

My mind felt clear.

I looked in the mirror and cried.

I knew I was gonna win.

Week five, the red dress from Cabo.

The one from when he still looked at me.

Zipped all the way up.

I felt like a woman again.

Week six, Gina called his agency.

Casting for the women over 50 line.

30 spots to fill.

I said, I can't.

She said, the universe just put you where you can do the most damage.

Girl, go.

I wore the red dress.

I walked into the lobby.

The woman he used to sleep with at lunch.

And there she was behind the desk.

Running the casting.

I almost threw up right there.

She saw me and froze.

Deer in headlights.

They called my name.

He was behind the camera.

He looked up and just stopped.

He never lowered the camera.

I didn't smile.

I hit my mark.

And I looked right down his lens.

The way she did in the video.

He called my name at the elevator.

Said it like a question.

Lisa?

Lisa.

I let the doors close.

Two days later, I booked it.

The over 50 line.

His agency's campaign.

First day of the shoot, she was in the chair next to mine.

26 with puppy dog eyes.

She leaned over.

I'm sorry.

I looked at her.

For what?

For all of it.

I had to ask.

What are you using?

And I told her.

She ordered it right there in the chair.

Here's what I know now.

I thought I was the problem.

Too old.

Too slow.

Too soft.

Too bloated.

I wasn't the problem.

I was full.

30 years of waste.

Nobody told me how to drain.

He didn't cheat because I got old.

He cheated because he's weak.

Because he wanted the girl in the pictures.

And I let myself believe I couldn't be her anymore.

But I drained it.

And I came back at 51.

I walked into his agency and booked a job.

A billboard on Sunset Boulevard.

Right next to hers.

If you're the wife in the minivan.

The tired one.

The one people stopped wondering about.

Maybe you've tried the fasts and the shakes.

Wore the Spanx under the dress.

The pamphlet from your doctor.

Don't let them talk you into the patch.

The shot.

When your body just needs help draining.

Haven & Spool castor oil pack.

You wrap it around your belly every night while you sleep.

The ricinoleic acid opens your drainage channels.

When your body feels supported.

It lets go of what it's been holding.

One pack every night.

Feels like a warm hug.

It's called Haven & Spool.

50% off right now.

30-day money back guarantee.

Six weeks.

That's all it took for me.

If you still see the button below.

Grab it.
